node.title: Arbitrary-arity list closure from the base crossing
node.statement: If an admissible row has a base-code adjacent crossing L_1(a0)>B*>=L_1(a0+1), B*=floor(|F|/2^128), then every interleaving arity m>=1 has the same adjacent crossing. The safe equality follows from list_subsqrt_interleaving_collapse because B*^2<|F| under |F|<2^256; diagonal tuples preserve the unsafe witness. This consumes only the m=1 instance of list_adjacency_closing.
node.notes: CONDITIONAL CLOSE 2026-07-12: arbitrary arity is no longer an independent red leaf. The general projection-collision theorem gives L_m=L_1 whenever L_1^2<|F|. The prior codegree, support-census, and extension-field routes remain proved evidence but are not required premises.
